findings.title: Team admin check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner`. Legitimate team admins who are not owners (and owners who are not admins) are rejected. Combined with the `?? 0` teamId fallback, the check is also meaningless for non-team bookings. It should be an OR, and only evaluated when a teamId exists.

findings.title: Any attendee may add guests to a booking
findings.body: Authorization grants access to any attendee, matched only by the user's email. An existing guest can therefore add arbitrary new attendees, who then receive emails and calendar invites. Emails are also compared without normalizing case. Permission should be limited to the organizer or team admins.

findings.title: Guest emails not case-normalized for dedupe and blacklist
findings.body: The blacklist is lowercased but guests are not, so `Foo@x.com` bypasses a blacklisted `foo@x.com`. Duplicates inside the input list or differing only by case are also not removed, so the same guest can be created twice.

findings.title: Emails sent with unfiltered guest list
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input rather than `uniqueGuests`. Blacklisted or already-existing attendees are mis-classified: existing attendees listed in the input get the 'scheduled' email, and blacklisted addresses get emailed if they are matched. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

findings.title: Calendar update failure after DB write is unhandled
findings.body: The attendees are persisted before `updateCalendarAttendees`, which is not in a try/catch. If it throws, the mutation fails and no emails are sent, yet the guests are already saved, leaving the state inconsistent. Also the EventManager is built from the caller's credentials rather than the organizer's.

findings.title: Subject uses first attendee's name
findings.body: The subject uses `attendees[0].name`, which is not the new guest, and the new guests are created with an empty name. Guests with `name: ""` also render poorly in emails and the attendee list.

findings.title: Error message built from code and translated message
findings.body: `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` is always truthy, so the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback never applies. It also shows raw codes like FORBIDDEN to the user.
